models.name: Qwen2.5 0.5B (base)
models.description: A pretrained base model, NOT instruction-tuned - it continues text rather than following instructions, and has no chat template, so a chat UI will get completions rather than answers. Strengths: the smallest file in the catalog and near-instant to load. Weaknesses: not usable as an assistant without further fine-tuning, and no tool-call ability at all. Listed at the ticket owner's request; it does not meet the instruction-tuned gate.

models.name: Qwen3 0.6B
models.description: The smallest model here, and the one most likely to run on a modest phone. Q8_0 keeps quantization loss minimal, so quality is limited by model size rather than by rounding. Strengths: fast, small, understands the Qwen3 tool-call format, and handles short instructions and simple single-step tool calls. Weaknesses: it is a 0.6B model - it loses track of long conversations, invents API details, and multi-step reasoning is unreliable. Treat it as a demo of the pipeline rather than a coding assistant.

models.name: Qwen3.5 0.8B
models.description: The newest and smallest capable model in this catalog, and the one to try first on a low-memory phone. Strengths: about half a gigabyte on disk, a very large published context window, and a current-generation post-trained Qwen with the tool-call format the family is known for. Weaknesses: at 0.8B parameters its reasoning and factual recall are shallow, and the advertised 256k context is theoretical on a phone - the KV cache for anything near it will not fit, so keep conversations short.

models.name: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct
models.description: Meta's smallest instruct model, widely used and well documented. Strengths: solid short-form instruction following for its size, a large published context, and a chat template every runtime understands. Weaknesses: the Llama 3.2 Community Licence carries use restrictions and the upstream Meta repo is access-gated, so this is not a fully-open model; tool use at 1B is unreliable. Listed at the ticket owner's request despite the licence gate.

models.name: SmolLM2 360M Instruct
models.publisher: Hugging Face TB - official GGUF release
models.description: Hugging Face's smallest instruct model, fully open with a public training recipe. Strengths: tiny, Apache-2.0 on both sides, instruction-tuned, and Q8_0 so quantization costs nothing. Weaknesses: an 8k context window - half the ticket's 16k floor - so long files or conversations will not fit, and at 360M parameters answers are short and often wrong. Listed at the ticket owner's request despite the context gate.

models.name: H2O Danube3 500M (base)
models.description: H2O's small pretrained model, Apache-2.0. A base model, NOT instruction-tuned, so it continues text instead of answering, and it has an 8k context window. Strengths: very small, permissively licensed, trained on a well-described corpus. Weaknesses: unusable as an assistant as shipped, no chat template, no tool use, and below the 16k context floor. Listed at the ticket owner's request; it meets neither the instruction-tuned nor the context gate.

models.name: OLMo 2 1B Instruct
models.publisher: Ai2 (Allen Institute for AI) - official GGUF release
models.description: Ai2's smallest instruct model and the most open one here: weights, training data, code and training recipe are all public, so it is the one to choose when the question is how a model was made. Strengths: Apache-2.0, an official GGUF from Ai2 itself, and a chat template. Weaknesses: a 4k context window - the smallest in this catalog - so only short files and short conversations fit; at about 1.5B parameters with Q4_K_M rounding it is weak at code and multi-step reasoning, and its model card claims no tool-call support. Listed at the ticket owner's request despite the context gate; the GGUF repository also declares no licence of its own.

models.name: Granite 4.0 1B
models.description: IBM's small instruct model, the dense (all-attention) variant rather than the hybrid Mamba one, so it runs on any recent llama.cpp. Strengths: Apache-2.0 on the model and the official GGUF, a large published context, and IBM trained it for tool calling and instruction following. Weaknesses: despite the name it is 1.6B parameters, so it is one of the larger downloads here and slower on a mid-range phone; the 128k context is theoretical on a phone because the KV cache will not fit; and at Q4_K_M it still invents APIs and loses multi-step reasoning.

models.name: SmolLM2 1.7B Instruct
models.publisher: Hugging Face TB - official GGUF release
models.description: The largest SmolLM2, from Hugging Face, with open training data and a public recipe. Strengths: Apache-2.0 on both sides, an official 4-bit GGUF, and clearly better answers than the 360M sibling - it is the general-purpose pick among the fully open models here. Weaknesses: an 8k context window, half the ticket's 16k floor, so long files or conversations will not fit; about 1 GB to download and slower than the sub-1B models on a mid-range phone; tool calls at this size are unreliable. Listed at the ticket owner's request despite the context gate.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B Instruct
models.description: The only model here trained specifically on code, and the one to pick for help with Kotlin and Java. Strengths: noticeably better at code syntax and less prone to inventing APIs than the general chat models in this catalog, a 32k context window, a chat template with the Qwen tool-call format, and Apache-2.0 on both the model and the official GGUF. Weaknesses: the largest download here at about 1 GB, and it needs more memory than the sub-1B models, so it is slower on a mid-range phone; at 1.5B parameters with Q4_K_M rounding it still gets multi-step reasoning and less common libraries wrong, and it is weaker at general conversation than at code.
